ghost_identification.description: Complete identification of the ghost forms surviving level-lowering
ghost_identification.ghost_1: 24.a ⊗ χ₂ (twist by χ₂, the Kronecker symbol (2/·))
ghost_identification.ghost_2: 24.a ⊗ χ₋₂ (twist by χ₋₂, the Kronecker symbol (-2/·))
ghost_identification.verification: 100% trace match for all primes 5 ≤ p ≤ 200
ghost_identification.method: Backwards base change from Q(√5) to Q with twist comparison
key_computation: Trace match at ℓ=11: a₁₁(ghost) = 0, a₁₁(24.a⊗χ₂) = χ₂(11)·(-2) = (-1)·(-2) = 0 ✓

gap_analysis.GAP_B_3_div_a: OPEN — this is the remaining obstacle
gap_analysis.gap_B_details: When 3|a, the conductor analysis at primes above 3 loses its bite

route_a_analysis.method: Local conductor mismatch at π = √5 (ramified in Q(√5))
route_a_analysis.key_correction: Wild ramification at char 5 is INVISIBLE in mod-7 representations. Pro-5 groups map trivially to GL₂(F₇) since 5 ∤ |GL₂(F₇)| = 2016.

sub_cases.5_not_div_abc: FAILS — both Frey and ghost have f_π = 0 (good reduction)
sub_cases.5_div_b: SUCCEEDS — multiplicative reduction forces f_π ≥ 1, and 7 ∤ (Norm(π)-1) = 4
sub_cases.5_div_a: NEEDS ANALYSIS — pole in t₀ requires Tate algorithm

route_a_analysis.conclusion: Route A handles 5|b and 5|c sub-cases only. Generic case 5 ∤ abc is open.

route_b2_analysis.method: Multi-Frey using BOTH E₃⁺ and E₃⁻ simultaneously
route_b2_analysis.status: HEURISTIC EVIDENCE but NOT a proof

key_data.but: Expected survivors = ∏(joint_count) > 0; the ghosts are real modular forms

route_b2_analysis.obstacle: Pure trace counting over F_ℓ doesn't use the S-unit constraint that t₀ = -b⁵/a³ with a³ + b⁵ = c⁷. The multi-Frey method in the paper likely uses the RELATIONSHIP between the two curves through the shared parameter t₀, not just independent trace matching.

e3_minus_ghost_traces.description: Traces of E₃⁻ at ghost parameters (integral model y² = x³ - 48x - 160)
e3_minus_ghost_traces.sample_traces: a₅=4, a₇=3, a₁₁=-4, a₁₃=-1, a₁₇=4, a₁₉=-1

route_d_analysis.status: STRONGLY SUGGESTED but not fully proven
route_d_analysis.ghost_reason: 24.a has isogeny degrees {1,2,3,4,6,8}; 7 is absent → no 7-isogeny
route_d_analysis.remaining: Need to check X₀(7) parametrization over Q(√5) to rule out 7-isogeny without 7-torsion. This is a finite computation.

what_we_need.primary: Confirmation that the ghost forms (24.a ⊗ χ±₂) are indeed the complete set of forms at the lowered level, and computational verification using Magma's ModularForms/HilbertModularForms machinery.
what_we_need.secondary: The multi-Frey elimination technique from §3 of the paper: how exactly does the paper use both E₃⁺ and E₃⁻ to close the case? Our trace-counting approach doesn't produce a clean contradiction.
what_we_need.tertiary: The 5|a sub-case from Route A: what does the Tate algorithm give for E₃⁺(-b⁵/a³) at π = √5 when 5|a?

our_contribution.ghost_identification: First explicit identification of ghost forms as 24.a ⊗ χ±₂
our_contribution.route_a_correction: Identified that wild ramification at char 5 vanishes mod 7
our_contribution.honest_assessment: Convergence at 0.90 — close but not closed
